gaps.sentence: ___ his age, he still plays football every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite his age' — noun phrase after despite.

gaps.sentence: He passed the oral exam ___ the fact that he had barely revised.
gaps.explanation: 'The fact that' turns the clause into a noun phrase, which 'despite' requires.

gaps.sentence: The drug is remarkably effective. ___, it has almost no side effects.
gaps.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces an additional point supporting the same claim.

gaps.sentence: ___ the theory is elegant, the data simply don't support it.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' grants the fact (the theory is elegant) before contradicting it.

gaps.sentence: They behaved ___ nothing at all had happened.
gaps.explanation: 'As if + past perfect' signals that the comparison is contrary to fact.

gaps.sentence: Bring a thermos ___ the tea tent closes at noon.
gaps.explanation: 'In case' = as a precaution against something happening.

gaps.sentence: ___ answering my question directly, he changed the subject.
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + -ing' highlights the action that did not happen.

gaps.sentence: ___ his leg was strapped up, the captain insisted on playing.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' intensifies the concession before a full clause.
